key_moments.title: Ireland scientists have found out how and why COVID-19 patients develop blood clots
The study was done by Researchers from Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland (RCSI) University of Medicine and Health Sciences
The study found that the balance between Von Willebrand Factor (VWF) and ADAMTS13 is severely disrupted in patients with severe COVID-19 infection
The researchers took and examined blood samples from patients with Covid-19 in the Beaumont Hospital Intensive Care Unit in Dublin
The researchers then compared the blood of COVID-19 patients with non-COVID patients
The researchers also identified other changes in the proteins that caused a drop in the ADAMTS13
According to previous research, blood clotting is a major cause of death in COVID-19 patients

related_questions.question: Does drinking water prevent blood clots?

text_blocks.snippet: While drinking water doesn't directly prevent blood clots, it's crucial for maintaining proper blood flow and overall health, which can indirectly help reduce the risk of blood clots. Dehydration can increase the risk of blood clots, so staying hydrated by drinking enough water is important, according to GoodRx and Wellow.
snippet_highlighted_words: drinking water doesn't directly prevent blood clots

list.snippet: Maintains healthy blood viscosity: Water helps keep your blood at a healthy consistency, making it easier to circulate.
Reduces dehydration risk: Dehydration can thicken your blood, making it more prone to clotting.
Supports overall health: Proper hydration is essential for various bodily functions, including blood circulation.

text_blocks.snippet: Other important factors for blood clot prevention:

list.snippet: Staying active: Regular exercise helps improve blood flow and prevent clots.
Avoiding prolonged immobility: If you're sitting for long periods, get up and move around regularly.
Managing weight: Maintaining a healthy weight reduces the risk of blood clots, according to the Laser Vascular Center.
Quitting smoking: Smoking increases the risk of blood clots.
Consulting your doctor: If you have risk factors or concerns, consult with your doctor for personalized advice.
